headline: Local Texas regulators approved well-water permits for part of Amazon's planned $10 billion data center campus near Houston, over objections from nearby residents.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the permits were issued on 8 Sep 2026, before the 2 Oct window, so the news is stale.
importance_line: Neighbors on private wells in Wharton County are most affected; this clears one step for Amazon, but cooling water and electricity needs are unsettled, and a judge found residents could not show their wells would be harmed.
summary: The Houston Chronicle reports that a local groundwater district approved permits on 8 Sep 2026 letting Amazon pump up to 78.2 million gallons of well water over two and a half years for restrooms, construction crews and fire protection at its planned data center campus in Wharton County, Texas. The permits do not cover the surface water the campus would need for cooling, and the Lower Colorado River Authority says Amazon has not yet applied for those permits.
notes: Underlying permit decision dated 8 Sep 2026; the Chronicle reported it on 2 Oct 2026.
